enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
438 AM MST Thu Nov 12 2026

...New AVIATION, FIRE WEATHER...

.KEY MESSAGES... Updated at 946 PM MST Tue Nov 10 2026

 - Dry conditions with seasonable temperatures.

 - Next system arrives Friday afternoon, bringing rain chances and 
   high elevation snow through Saturday afternoon.

 - Slight chance of showers Tuesday night. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 946 PM MST Wed Nov 11 2026

Upper ridge continues to build over the Great Basin and Desert 
Southwest, ahead of a deepening Pacific trough still off the west 
coast of the US. Meanwhile the sub-tropical jet remains active with 
deep layered sub-tropical moisture, but feature will remain well 
south of our area. Thus the upper ridge is the dominating playa over 
tonight into early Friday, with mostly clear skies and seasonable 
temperatures. 

Friday and Saturday...Pacific trough finally moves onshore as it 
continues to dig as very strong polar jet dives down the back side 
of the trough. As the Gulf of Alaska upper low weakens, a closed off 
low will form at the bottom of the trough and swing across the 
northern Baja Friday afternoon. This low will contain a decent 
amount of moisture and all three of GFS/ECMWF/RRFS showing low able 
to tap a bit of the sub-tropical moisture over Mexico. Good chance 
for showers to develop and make it as far east as the RG Valley by 
late Friday afternoon. GFS still shows good cold air aloft (about 5C 
deg cooling at 500mb), which should lead to decent instability with 
very modest CAPES. Because of this, an isolated thunderstorm will be 
possible with the showers. With the upper low tracking across 
northern Mexico or far southern New Mexico Friday night along with 
the surface cold front, showers will spread east over the rest of 
the area. Expect broad area of .25-.50 of rainfall across the area, 
with a few spots maybe hitting 1.0 inch with a thunderstorm. 
Most/all showers should be done in the east by mid day Saturday as 
the low quickly moves into central Texas. Snow levels will remain 
high, but an inch or so of snow is possible above 8500 ft. Rapidly 
moving upper low associated with the polar jet moves in right behind 
the exiting low but will track across Colorado Saturday night. Rain 
chances should remain north of the CWA, but could see some breezy 
winds Saturday night.

Sunday and Monday...short wave ridge sweeps in Sunday behind the 
exiting lows. Expect mostly clear skies again, but temperatures will 
be cool, a bit below normal, behind the cold front.

Tuesday and Wednesday...next Pacific system moves in with the low 
tracking across SoCal and Arizona. Both GFS/ECMWF similar with the 
track but ECMWF about 6-10 hours faster than GFS. Rain chances 
increase as early as Tuesday mid day and are likely done by mid day 
Wednesday. Temperatures will remain below normal. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 437 AM MST Thu Nov 12 2026

VFR conditions today with SKC and dry conditions. Light winds 
through the period generally AOB 10KT.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 437 AM MST Thu Nov 12 2026

Low fire weather concerns through the week ahead. Min RH values stay 
above critical thresholds each day. RH values will be 25-35% in the 
lowlands and 30-40% in the area mountains today. Rain chances return 
Friday afternoon with continued showers overnight before exiting 
Saturday. Min RHs increase Friday to 40-50% in the lowlands and 45-
55% in the area mountains. Lowland min RHs stay the same Saturday 
but mountain RHs increase to 60-90%. Min RHs decrease again Sunday 
due to dry conditions but will be on the increase again early next 
week due to another round of rain that's expected to arrive Tuesday 
and Wednesday.

20 foot winds will stay light each afternoon at 5-10 mph except for 
Saturday afternoon as winds will be breezy with speeds generally 10-
20 mph. Temperatures will stay near normal today and tomorrow 
becoming below normal Saturday through mid-week next week.

&&
